## Course overview

Welcome to [DATASCI 151](https://github.com/danilofreire/datasci151-summer)! This course introduces data analysis and statistical computing with Python and SQL. Please have a look at [the course syllabus](https://danilofreire.github.io/datasci151-summer/syllabus.html) and the [lecture schedule](https://danilofreire.github.io/datasci151-summer/lectures.html) for more information. You will find a brief overview of the course below.

## Contact information

- Name: Danilo Freire
- Email: <danilo.freire@emory.edu>
- Office hours: by appointment, so please email me to schedule a meeting
- Canvas: course announcements, Teams meeting links and grades

## Repository structure

This website gives an overview of the course, but all the materials live in our GitHub repository at <https://github.com/danilofreire/datasci151-summer>. The repository has the following folders and files:

- [`assignments/`](https://github.com/danilofreire/datasci151-summer/tree/main/assignments): all course assignments
- [`lectures/`](https://github.com/danilofreire/datasci151-summer/tree/main/lectures): lecture slides, notebooks and code
- [`tutorials/`](https://github.com/danilofreire/datasci151-summer/tree/main/tutorials): step-by-step guides for the tools we use in the course
- [`syllabus.pdf`](https://github.com/danilofreire/datasci151-summer/blob/main/syllabus.pdf): the course syllabus in PDF format

The links above open the folders and files in the repository. To see the rendered pages on this website, please use the navigation bar at the top.

## Course content

### Lectures

We will meet online via Teams every weekday from May 11th to May 28th, 2027, from 11:00am to 12:20pm EDT. You will find the meeting link on Canvas. The [course schedule](https://danilofreire.github.io/datasci151-summer/lectures.html) lists all topics, dates and suggested readings, and the lecture materials are in the [lectures folder](https://github.com/danilofreire/datasci151-summer/tree/main/lectures) of the repository.

Each folder has an HTML presentation or a Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`) with code examples and explanations, plus any datasets or other files we use in class.

### Assignments and quizzes

You will complete five assignments and three quizzes during the course. I will post the assignments in the [`assignments/`](https://github.com/danilofreire/datasci151-summer/tree/main/assignments) folder as the course goes on, and each quiz will have its own GitHub repository. I will also announce them in class and on Canvas. The syllabus and the lecture schedule have all due dates and submission guidelines.

### Tutorials

The [Tutorials](tutorials.qmd) page has step-by-step guides for the tools we use in the course. Please have a look at them before our first class, as they will help you get started.

### JupyterLite

You can run Python directly in your browser at <https://danilofreire.github.io/datasci151-summer/jupyter>, with no installation required. It runs on [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org), a version of Python for the browser that comes with pandas, numpy, matplotlib and the other libraries we use in the course. It is useful for quick experiments when you do not have Anaconda at hand.

## Course requirements

- Prerequisites: none, only a willingness to learn and try new tools!
- Software: [Anaconda distribution of Python 3.x](https://www.anaconda.com/), [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/), [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/) and [GitHub Desktop](https://github.com/apps/desktop)
- Please also create an educational account on [GitHub](https://education.github.com/)

## Grading

- Assignments (5x): 50%
- Quizzes (3x): 50%
